text: The service facts are taken from Template and Rules v1 R4 and the S9 story set of this folder because the S9 context pack and the S9 module extracts are absent: schema and login rwb_partner, base /api/recovery/partner/v1, topic rwb.partner.events.v1 with retry and .dlt topics, event names rwb.partner.<Event>.v1, queue rwb-partner, namespace rwb-recovery and Java package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner.
why: The work package names the context pack as the authority for the service row, the ownership rows and the naming rules, and the file does not exist in this workspace, so the same facts have to come from a lower source in the precedence list.
read: The naming rule of R4 is mechanical on the short name partner; the ownership of partner, partner_user and partner_instruction is read from the S9 table rows of the sibling stories and from the field IDs DF-PRT and DF-REF the primary slice does not use; the service wave of Arch v5 is 4 and the story wave 1 comes from the W-MAP of EP01.
confirm: Solution architect, when the context pack is issued
impact: A correction of a naming fact would touch section 12.1 and section 13 of this story and no test.

text: The partner slice of RWB-E1-032 is the file-submission channel of the OCR intake: the submission row and its partner reference in rwb_partner, the case hint of the instruction, the acceptance record, the attach state read back from rwb-document, the reconcile Schedule and the read on SCR-35. The match, the store, the OCR, the classification, the extraction and the resolution of a held item stay with RWB-P5-E1032-APP.
why: The legacy story names partner files as an intake source and gives no partner-service duty, the work package marks this story secondary with no legacy AC, and the two services must not both write a document or an intake item.
read: The boundary follows the data each service owns: the firm, the instruction and its case ID are S9's, the file and the intake item are P5's; the case hint is a value on the event and never a case table read.
confirm: Business analyst, S9, and the owner of RWB-P5-E1032-APP
impact: No document, intake item or case row is written twice, and a change of the boundary would move work between two stories and touch no other service.

text: The story keeps wave 1 from the W-MAP of EP01 although Arch v5 puts rwb-partner in wave 4, the release date 30 November 2026 is copied unchanged and marked tentative, and no date is raised as a gap.
why: Template and Rules R5.6 keeps the earlier W-MAP wave and asks for one conflict gap per service and business epic, and R7.1 carries the story wave into the metadata.
read: The wave row of the metadata copies the work package, the release row carries the legacy date with the tentative mark, and section 3 states the conflict so the delivery plan can sequence the partner channel with Epic 1.
impact: The partner channel of the intake ships with Epic 1 while the rest of the service follows in wave 4; the date does not move.

text: The seven platform CON rows the DP table adds (E1027, E1042, E1043, TE006, E1071, E1044, N001) are the shared platform baseline of wave 0 and the two list contracts arrive through the client library, so they add no H row and no C row to this story, and the metadata keeps the plan's empty H row and its single C row.
why: The work package fixes the H and C rows for this key, and the platform libraries are published once for every service of the wave rather than per story.
read: Section 13 names each pattern with the row R5.5 gives it and states which of them is a platform baseline; the build uses the libraries the service template ships and blocks on none of them.
confirm: Solution architect and the platform owner
impact: The lane stays at Day 1; if the plan owner records the seven rows as H, the ready row gains no date but the lane shows seven platform edges.

text: The two partner operations are this story's design choice on the service base (POST and GET /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/documents), the event is rwb.partner.PartnerDocumentSubmitted.v1, the activities are recordPartnerDocument and reconcilePartnerIntake, and the document-hub intake creation is consumed as the operation that creates an intake item although its path is unpublished; the S9 contract baseline publishes the shapes at the wave start.
why: No source publishes the operations, the event name, the event catalogue ID, the activity names or the intake creation, and the story cannot be built without a shape to build against.
read: The paths copy the instruction suffix of the sibling S9 operations onto the service base of DP-13; the shapes use the IntakeItem and match-state vocabulary of RWB-P5-E1032-CON; no API identifier is invented beyond the paths and every unpublished element carries the gap.
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-document contract owner and the S9 contract baseline owner
impact: A published shape replaces the paths in one section and no test logic; the event name change touches section 12.3 and the consumer fixture.

text: The acceptance of a partner file names a decision code and a version in force read as values, the intake bound and the two lists are read at their version, and none of the four is typed in code; the code, the bound and the parameter row are placeholders until the business lead loads them.
why: The legacy story fixes the three document-hub parameters and no partner parameter, names no decision code and gives no body bound, and the story must still record the acceptance and refuse an oversized file.
read: The record names the code and the version the parameters answer on the submitted date; the bound is read through DP-06 and the lists through DP-07; a missing row refuses the submission rather than defaulting a value.
confirm: Business lead, S9, and the data steward
impact: A partner file cannot be accepted before the rows exist, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour; no other service is affected.

text: The submission row is partner_intake in rwb_partner, created by this story's own Flyway step with the columns of section 11, and this service keeps no file: the file is hashed and handed to the document hub, and the row carries the intake item ID it answers.
why: The partner tables of the data model cannot hold a submission, no source states whether the partner service keeps a file, and the file and its retention belong to rwb-document.
read: The table name follows the legacy document_intake marker onto the owner's schema (DP-01); the unique key on instruction and hash carries R-UNI-40; no field ID is invented and the LDM row is the proposed fix of the gap.
impact: A change of the table name touches section 12.7 and the migration only; no file, no OCR text and no personal data is stored here.

text: AC1 to AC15 and TC-E1-032-01 to TC-E1-032-17 of the legacy story stay with RWB-P5-E1032-APP; this story carries seven new criteria and eight new test cases and executes no legacy test case, and the legacy identifiers appear once in section 16 so that no test loses its trace.
why: The work package gives this story an empty acceptance list with the full legacy test-case list, and R7.2 asks a story to keep the test cases of the criteria it owns.
read: The ownership is read from the data each criterion asserts: every legacy criterion asserts a document, an intake item, a case or a reviewer action, all of which are the primary slice's; this story asserts its own row, record, event, call and state only.
impact: The Test Cases master keeps one row per test and no test is duplicated or dropped; the RTM shows both slices against the same requirement rows.

text: The partner portal screen that submits a file is one of PRT-01 to PRT-04 and its exact number is a placeholder, and the reconcile Schedule keeps the legacy JOB-12 cadence of every 15 minutes in business hours.
why: No source numbers a document screen on the partner portal, while the legacy story fixes the cadence of the intake job that this channel joins.
read: The cadence is copied from the legacy story and not chosen; the screen is named as a range and the field list is left to the platform edge story.
confirm: UX lead and the platform edge owner
impact: A screen number correction touches section 15 only; the cadence change would touch the Schedule row and one test.

text: No approval stop was taken: FSD S9 and TSD S9 are not approved in this run and the story is Draft (realignment v1); no human verification was requested and no later lifecycle stage was started.
why: The realignment run proceeds without human approval and a missing status is recorded as an assumption rather than raised as a question.
read: The status row of the metadata carries Draft (realignment v1); the sources used are the legacy story, the S9 story set and Template and Rules v1, and no approval statement is invented for any of them.
impact: The story is buildable but not approved; the approval step of the normal lifecycle is deferred to the later verification loop.
